mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% may indicate a tight labor market, potentially leading to inflationary pressures and negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate stays below 4% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of the 20-day horizon cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases and the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is already high, it may signal inflationary pressures that could negatively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both CPIAUCSL increases and FEDFUNDS are high but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of the 20-day horizon cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) indicates strong supply and economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If Industrial Production increases but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) suggests a strong labor market, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the 5-day horizon cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real sales (RSAFS) indicates weak demand, which could negatively impact S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by more than 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: If real sales decline but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of the 20-day horizon cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a low unemployment rate (UNRATE) together indicate strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both housing starts increase and unemployment is low but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the 60-day horizon cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary tightening cycle may increase borrowing costs and negatively impact S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 25bps in the last meeting
failure_condition: If the Federal Funds rate increases but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of the 20-day horizon cases.
